title: Gaming setup
description: Steam plus optional performance tools (GameMode and MangoHud). Needs the [multilib] repository enabled in /etc/pacman.conf.
author: Tux Store

download_mb.label: Download size
download_mb.shell: pacman -Si steam 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Download Size/ {v=$4; u=$5; if (u=="KiB") v/=1024; else if (u=="GiB") v*=1024; else if (u=="B") v/=1048576; t+=v} END {printf "%d\n", t+0.5}'

installed_mb.label: Installed size
installed_mb.shell: pacman -Si steam 2>/dev/null | awk '/^Installed Size/ {v=$4; u=$5; if (u=="KiB") v/=1024; else if (u=="GiB") v*=1024; else if (u=="B") v/=1048576; t+=v} END {printf "%d\n", t+0.5}'

info.note: Sizes are read from your package database. Packages you already have are skipped.

welcome.title: Gaming setup
message: Play games on Linux.
Steam comes from the [multilib] repository, so it must be enabled in /etc/pacman.conf. If it is not, this add-on stops and tells you.
The performance set adds GameMode (CPU/GPU tuning while a game runs) and MangoHud (an FPS overlay).

choose.title: What do you want to install?
choose.message: You can run this again later to add more.

command.label: Checking your system…
shell: [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] || { echo "Tux Store is running as root. Start it as a normal user; it asks for the password only when needed."; exit 0; }
for t in pkexec pacman; do
command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "The required tool '$t' is missing."; exit 0; }
[ ! -e /var/lib/pacman/db.lck ] || { echo "pacman is locked (/var/lib/pacman/db.lck exists). Another package manager may be running. Wait for it to finish, then try again."; exit 0; }

grep -q "^\[multilib\]" /etc/pacman.conf 2>/dev/null || { echo "The [multilib] repository is not enabled. Uncomment [multilib] and its Include line in /etc/pacman.conf, run pacman -Sy, then try again."; exit 0; }

command.label: Looking at what is already installed…
shell: pacman -Si "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue      # not in your repositories: handled below

commands.label: Removing the codec packages
shell: # Two passes: a package may only become removable after another one is gone.
if pacman -Rns --noconfirm "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "removed $p"; elif [ "$pass" = 2 ]; then echo "kept $p (other software needs it)"; fi
